messages.subject: Pcountopen dynamics
parts:
Hi guys,

Just wanted to first say that this group has been very helpful in answering a lot of the questions I’ve had while analysing my n mixture model data, so thank you!

I do have a couple of questions regarding the open population N-mixture model that I haven’t been able to find answers to, even after reading the vignettes and Dail & Madsen’s and Royle’s paper. I’m sorry if they’re daft questions, I’m fairly new to this:

1. Dynamics type eg. trend, ricker, gompertz: How do you decide on the right dynamics type? Is it by AIC? If so, some dynamics types make more sense biologically, such as ricker and Gompertz. My best performing model is a trend dynamics type, so what does that say about the population I’m studying? Is there a paper I can read more about this?

2. Initially, my best performing model was a Gompertz dynamics type, and the gamma was 0.508 and omega is 37.9. According to the vignette, this means my population growth rate is 0.508 and carrying capacity is 37.9. For carrying capacity, is it an average and do I multiply the value with the number of sites?

Would really appreciate any help in this, either by answering directly or pointing me in the right direction in terms of resources. Thanks again!

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: AW: [unmarked] Pcountopen dynamics
parts:
Dear Inuyasha (?),

 

I make a stab at your first question, anybody please correct me if you disagree or if I am wrong.

 

I find that in many situations, the most important criterion for model selection should be a combination of your biological insight and the goals of your modelling. So, if you think that density-dependent (DD) regulation is a strong feature of your population (of what ?), then I’d choose either ricker or gompertz and then do data-based selection between them using the AIC. Similarly, if you’re interested in DD and would like to estimate things like carrying capacity, then evidently you’d need a model that incorporates this feature.

 

On the other hand, if you’re just after some descriptive accommodation of population change and are not sure how close or far your population may be from a limit, then perhaps the simple trend model (which I think is simple exponential growth without DD) may be OK, and if it is preferred by AIC, then this may be the one to go with.

 

Not sure about your second question.

 

Best regards  --- Marc
